thread:
maya: heads-up, seeing a KV cache growth spike + continuous-batching stall on streaming workers in us-west-2. latency climbing and partial flushes failing. creating thread now. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED · Sev 1 · kv-cache/continuous-batch · 2468101212
alex: oncall here, linking traces + metrics. which tenant(s) impacted?
samir: acme-inc and a handful of small customers showing elevated 5xx for stream endpoints. error rate ~0.7% overall but spikes to 4-6% for some hosts.
nora: logs show many "partial flush failed: context cancelled" from batcher. stacktrace snippet attached below:
```
batcher.go:412: flushPartial -> error: context canceled
streaming_worker.go:229: writeTokens -> write queue drained unexpectedly
kv_cache.go:178: Set -> memUsage=12.4GB incr=2.1GB keys=8.3M
```
len: interesting — memory growth aligns with heavy prefix reuse patterns. I see continuous-batch window not trimming when KV eviction is triggered.
sre-ops: paging FYI, we've put this at SEV1. Please keep notes in this thread for handoff. PagerDuty alert linked.
maya: mitigation attempts so far: 1) toggled batcher_debug to log-only (no change), 2) rolled back latest batch config from 0.8 -> 0.6 for the canary pool (still warming), 3) disabled warm-prefix-caching flag for affected fleet (temporary).
alex: can we force a soft-eviction to cut mem growth? command suggestion: `curl -XPOST http://admin us-west-2/kv/evict?target=soft` — but need to coordinate with data safety.
samir: acme is on a dedicated capacity; suggest isolating their traffic to a fallback model to reduce streaming load. routing change prepared: `route set acme-inc -> model-128-fallback` (canary first).
nora: capturing metric diffs. current: kv_mem_rss: +42% last 15m, continuous_batch_queue_len: +320%, partial_flush_errors: 124 -> 987 in 10m.
incident-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: notify customer success for impacted tenants. CS alert sent to #customer-success.
len: found a suspicious regression in batch cadence logic — when kv eviction backpressure is applied, cadence timer jitter increases and the batcher stops issuing final flushes under contention. Repro locally with high prefix reuse.
maya: ok patch attempt: reduce max_batch_window_ms from 120 to 60, and add a guard to force flush when queue_len > 80% of target_batch_size. applying to canary now.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: maya/kv-batcher-cadence-fix -> canary (3 pods). ETA ~2m.
alex: ping when canary is up; we'll watch tailing logs and metrics.
(2m later)
deploy-bot: deploy success: maya/kv-batcher-cadence-fix -> canary (3 pods) · 2468101475
samir: initial canary looks good — partial_flush_errors dropped to single digits, latency down ~120ms p50 on canary hosts. kv mem growth slowed.
maya: rolling to 20% now.
(10m later)
alex: rolling 20 -> 60%. monitoring for regression.
nora: streaming token cadence on rolled hosts stabilized; we still see a couple hosts with flaky write queue stalls — maybe due to underlying worker GC. collecting heap profiles.
len: discovered older kernel VM setting on two hosts causing shorter file descriptor reuse windows — bumped ulimit and reaped file descriptors on those hosts. small throughput improvement.
samir: customer impact update for CS: Acme Inc saw degraded streaming from 15:06–15:28 UTC, errors peaked at 6% for them. we've isolated them to fallback capacity at 15:31 and errors subsided.
maya: open action items: 1) ship cadence guard + batch_window reduction to all fleets, 2) add metric alert for continuous_batch_queue_len > 200 for >2m, 3) add postmortem notes on prefix-cache eviction coordination.
alex: agree. also recommend backfill: add an automatic soft-eviction when memRSS > 10GB per shard for non-critical tenants. prioritize safety.
sre-ops: prepping oncall handoff at 16:00 UTC. please add any lingering context.
maya: added a brief summary to the runbook: "kv continuous-batch cadence stall — symptoms: rising kv memRSS, continuous_batch_queue_len spike, partial_flush context cancellations, streaming latency and 5xx. mitigation: batch_window reduce, cadence guard flush, soft-evict, routing fallback."
len: logging note: increased log-level to debug for batcher but rate-limited; we have sample traces saved under /artifacts/incident-2468101212/ for postmortem.
samir: CS note: notified Acme and two SMBs, they accepted that we mitigated and requested RCA within 48h.
alex: handing off to night oncall @nora for final watch and follow-up tomorrow. please keep this thread updated.
nora: acknowledged. I'll maintain until COB and start the postmortem draft. leaving a short checklist in the thread: 1) confirm new alerts fire on synthetic, 2) schedule root-cause deep-dive with ML infra and batcher owners, 3) validate no data loss for affected streams.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED · 2468104800 · condition: cadence guard rolled, canary -> 100% gradual, customer routing fallback applied, pending postmortem.
maya: thanks everyone. adding timeline + links to dashboards in the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
